story_text:
## Your e-bike, scooter, or power station can fail without warning.
Preion is a small early-warning device you set down next to the battery while it charges. It watches for the gases and heat of early cell failure and alerts your phone before smoke or flames, with up to 8-12 minutes of potential warning, so you can unplug and get people out.
## The setting up
How to set up Preion from start to finish.Peter demonstrates how to set up the device for use. Obviously, people don’t normally store bicycles on a table, we put ours there so you can see everything more clearly.In this video, we use a proprietary air/gas mixture with a 1% gas concentration, identical to the gases released during the early stages of thermal runaway. We’re using the Preion Pro in this video. The difference between the Pro and the Puppy is that the Pro includes an IoT SIM.
## Smoke is a late-stage warning.
You charge the scooter in the hallway because that is where it lives. The e-bike leans against the garage wall overnight. The power station sits by the skirting board, quietly filling. A smoke alarm is built to wait for particles in the air, the late stage of a fire you can already see. Lithium batteries fail earlier than that, and quieter. Preion is built for that earlier stage: the chemistry inside a failing cell, before smoke has anything to report.
## Battery fires don't start with fire.
Inside a healthy lithium-ion cell, a thin protective layer keeps the chemistry calm. Damage, aging, overcharging, or a knock can crack that layer. The cell starts releasing gases you cannot smell on purpose: hydrogen, carbon monoxide, VOCs. It also builds heat you cannot see. Those reactions feed themselves. In minutes they can race toward venting or fire. Miners once took a canary underground because toxic gas arrives before smoke. Preion is that idea without the bird: a sensor for the gases a failing battery gives off, while you still have time.
## Preion watches the air around a charging battery.
Preion does not replace your charger, your smoke alarm, or a fire extinguisher. It is the device you place next to the lithium battery you already own. It reads the air and the heat around the cells. If the pattern looks like early failure, it warns you, with up to 8-12 minutes of potential warning before visible smoke. That is time to cut power, open a door, and get people out.
## Monitor. Detect. Analyze. Alert.
Preion sits near the pack and continuously reads gas composition, temperature, and humidity. Dedicated sensors watch for hydrogen and VOC signatures, rapid heat rise, and environmental patterns tied to cell failure. Then the system compares the combined pattern to known failure signatures, so ordinary off-gassing does not have to become a 3 a.m. panic. If the pattern matches a genuine precursor, you get an alert.
## The warning hits your phone while you can still act.
You will not always be standing next to the charger. When Preion detects a precursor event, it does not send one notification and hope. Alerts escalate automatically: a push in the Preion app, then SMS, then an automated voice call until someone acknowledges. Dual Wi-Fi and a built-in IoT SIM keep the device reporting even if your home network drops.

## Set it down where you charge.
No tools. No installer. Unbox it, power it on, pair the app, and put it on the deck, the shelf, or the garage floor, wherever the battery rests. Charging is when most lithium failures begin. That is exactly when Preion watches closest.
## Keep your smoke alarms. Add the missing layer.
Preion is not a smoke detector. It is not a sprinkler. It will not put out a fire. Keep every alarm you already have. Preion is an extra early-warning layer built specifically for lithium battery failure, so those alarms may never have to go off for this particular risk.
## Lithium batteries moved into the house.
The garage is now a charging room. The hallway holds a scooter because the apartment has no shed. Power stations and home batteries sit indoors, next to coats, shoes, and the door you need in an emergency. Packs got denser. Failures got faster. The detection around them barely changed. Early warning is a household problem now, not a factory problem you can ignore.
## Designed, engineered, and tested in Hungary.
Péter Varsányi and Balázs Bálint started Preion after watching how late a typical smoke alarm reacts to a real battery fire. Péter leads the company. Balázs built the hardware and the software. The work is in Hungary: multiple functional prototypes, a live mobile app, cloud connectivity, and real-time alerts, not a slide deck. The project was presented on the Hungarian show Cápák Között and nominated for a Raiffeisen Bank special award in the Value Creation category.
## Help us build the first production run.
Kickstarter is how we tool the first production run and put a finished Preion in the first homes that need it. In the box: the monitoring device, a USB cable, a quick-start guide, and the companion app. Unbox it, pair it, set it down next to the battery. Get the warning before smoke.
## How is Preion different from a smoke detector?
Smoke is often a late-stage warning. Smoke detectors react to particles in the air. Preion monitors the gas, thermal, and environmental signals released during the earliest stages of lithium battery failure, often well before visible smoke appears.
## Is Preion a replacement for my smoke detector?
No. Preion is an additional early-warning layer specifically for lithium battery failures. It works alongside your existing smoke and heat detectors. The goal is to alert you before they ever need to.
## What types of batteries can Preion monitor?
Environments with lithium-ion and lithium-polymer batteries: e-bikes, scooters, power tools, portable power stations, and home energy storage.
## Does Preion put out fires?
No. It warns you. Keep a proper extinguisher and a way out. Unplug if it is safe to do so.
## How do I receive alerts?
Alerts escalate automatically: push notifications in the Preion app, SMS, and automated voice calls to your registered numbers.
## Do I need an electrician?
No. Place Preion next to the battery, power it from USB, and pair the app.
## Where is Preion being developed?
In Hungary, by a small team focused on lithium battery safety. Hardware prototypes, the mobile app, and cloud infrastructure are already operational.
risks: We've already cleared the hardest part: the technology. Multiple working prototypes are built and validated, our mobile app and cloud monitoring are live, and our detection models have completed field testing. The remaining work is manufacturing at scale and worldwide fulfillment. Our main challenges are supply-chain timing for sensor and electronic components and safety certification in each market. We're mitigating these by working with established manufacturing partners, ordering long-lead components early, and building realistic buffers into our timeline. As a team of hardware, embedded, and IT engineers focused solely on lithium-battery safety, we'll keep backers updated transparently at every step.
